go_no_go_rationale:
DESCOPE — keep the defect-fix and decision spine, gate everything downstream behind a cheap measured go/no-go, and stop treating 83.2-83.6 as a committed build.

Three independent reasons, all measured against the live repo rather than inherited from the corpus.

(1) THE PLAN IS CURRENTLY UNRUNNABLE FOR REASONS UNRELATED TO ALPHA. `backend/backtest/` contains ZERO imports of `backend/tools/screener.py`; backtest candidate selection runs its own formula at `backend/backtest/candidate_selector.py:186-206`, so all 14 `apply_*_to_score` overlays are LIVE-ONLY and a 15th theme overlay cannot produce a DSR or a PBO at all (breaks 83.5 and 83.6). `scripts/risk/gauntlet.py` — which 83.5's own name instructs us to reuse — is dry-run-stub-only by design ("dry-run is currently the ONLY implemented mode"; `run()` raises NotImplementedError otherwise), and `backend/backtest/gauntlet/evaluator.py` checks exactly four drawdown/kill conditions with zero DSR, zero PBO, zero cost, zero incumbent. `_NUMERIC_FEATURES` (37 entries, verified, zero news-derived) is a column FILTER at `backtest_engine.py:712`; values come only from `historical_data.build_feature_vector`'s three BQ caches, so 83.4's list-append is a silent no-op without a new data path.

(2) THE GATE THE CORPUS OPTIMISED AGAINST IS THE WRONG ONE. `backend/autoresearch/gate.py:21-30` is the module that actually joins the two: `min_dsr=0.95`, `max_pbo=0.20`, `min_pbo_trials=10`. Every one of the 8 research lenses states PBO<=0.50 — that figure is `backend/services/promotion_gate.py:37`, a different (live allocation-staging, PSR-based) decision. So every feasibility verdict in the corpus was computed against a ceiling 2.5x too permissive. Worse, the exposed `mcp__pyfinagent-risk__pbo_check` calls RAW `compute_pbo` (`risk_server.py:142-143`), which returns 0.0 — the best possible value, passing every ceiling — whenever T < S*2 = 32 (`analytics.py:297-298`); `compute_pbo_checked` exists at `analytics.py:208` precisely to refuse this and is not wired in. And `gate.py`'s minimum-trials refusal is bypassed entirely when a producer omits `pbo_n_trials`. A short-sample theme candidate evaluated through the obvious tool gets a silent false PASS.

(3) THE ALPHA CLAIM IS WEAKER THAN THE PHASE ASSUMES, AND ITS P0 DATA SOURCE IS BLOCKED. The single pro-thesis result (6.96%/yr narrative alpha, t=2.53) is statistically ZERO in its own first half (2013-2017: alpha 1.00%, t=0.20), rests on a proprietary MKT MediaStats series two of its three authors are affiliated with, and only 1.46%/yr of it is genuinely cross-SECTOR. Beneficiary selection by naming or media coverage is a published NULL and is the same rule that produces -0.50%/mo for 60 months post-ETF-launch. Meanwhile Alpha Vantage — which four lenses and 83.0(c) make the P0 backfill — is licence-restricted to "personal, non-commercial use" with "investment analysis, research, testing" NAMED as commercial, measured at 25 requests/day, with a >=19x archive-vs-live density discontinuity that is point-in-time disqualifying independent of licence.

WHY NOT `do_not_build`: 83.0 is a genuine, independently-justified loss-prevention defect — `NEWS_SCREEN_ENABLED=true` moves the real book through `screener.py:334` while no corpus is persisted (`bq_writer._insert_rows` returns 0 and logs on any failure, including a missing table). Fixing that is money-positive regardless of whether any theme signal ever ships. And the go/no-go arithmetic itself has an unmeasured input — trial-Sharpe dispersion V, which swings the required Sharpe 2.3x (1.38 at V=0.25 to 3.18 at V=1.00) and which Lens 5 and Lens 7 silently set to DIFFERENT values (~0.30 vs 0.50) to reach OPPOSITE conclusions. Killing the phase on an unmeasured parameter would be the same error the corpus made.

WHY NOT `proceed_with_revisions`: that implies 83.2-83.6 survive roughly intact. They do not. 83.3's phase-kill test ("can the map name memory from an AI theme") is the exact selection rule the evidence refutes; 83.5 targets a stub; 83.6 is downstream of both and additionally ships a boost overlay into a `sign_safe_overlays=False` default that INVERTS boosts on negative composites — i.e. it would DEMOTE theme beneficiaries in precisely the four drawdown regimes the phase exists to capture.

THE DESCOPE: keep 83.0 (retargeted off Alpha Vantage). Add three P0 defect steps that are money-positive standalone (news timestamp PIT, sector lookahead, PBO false-PASS). Rewrite 83.1 as the write-up of THIS completed research with the CORRECTED thresholds pinned to source. Add 83.1.1 as the actual go/no-go — a measured, near-free arithmetic step with a kill rule pre-registered BEFORE the numbers exist. Add 83.1.2 to make overlays measurable at all. Everything from 83.2 onward hangs off 83.1.1's recorded verdict.
headline_findings: THE GATE IS PBO <= 0.20, NOT 0.50. Verified at backend/autoresearch/gate.py:21-30 — min_dsr=0.95, max_pbo=0.20, min_pbo_trials=10. All 8 research lenses state 0.50, which is backend/services/promotion_gate.py:37 (a different, live-allocation-staging, PSR-based decision). Every feasibility verdict in the corpus was computed against a ceiling 2.5x too loose. Additionally, gate.py's minimum-trials refusal is BYPASSED whenever a producer omits the pbo_n_trials key — a trial that never reports N is treated as legacy and promoted on a coarse statistic.

OVERLAYS CANNOT BE GATED AT ALL. `grep -rn 'from backend.tools.screener' backend/backtest/` returns NOTHING; backtest ranking is an independent formula at backend/backtest/candidate_selector.py:186-206 (mom*w + rsi*w + vol*w + sma*w). All 14 apply_*_to_score overlays are live-only and structurally invisible to run_backtest, so a 15th theme overlay can never produce a DSR or PBO. This alone makes 83.5 and 83.6 unactionable as written, independent of any alpha question.

THE GAUNTLET 83.5 IS TOLD TO REUSE IS A STUB. scripts/risk/gauntlet.py docstring: 'dry-run is currently the ONLY implemented mode'; run() raises NotImplementedError otherwise and the report writer refuses any report not labeled dry_run:true. backend/backtest/gauntlet/evaluator.py evaluates exactly four gates — per-regime drawdown ratio <= 2.0, forced_exits == 0, MC p99 ratio <= 2.0, MC breaches == 0 — containing zero DSR, zero PBO, zero cost, zero incumbent. The north-star gate does not exist as one joined runnable verdict anywhere; DSR lives at quant_optimizer.py:300, DSR+PBO at autoresearch/gate.py, PSR+PBO at services/promotion_gate.py, drawdown-only in the gauntlet.

THE EXPOSED PBO TOOL MANUFACTURES A PASS. backend/agents/mcp_servers/risk_server.py:142-143 calls RAW compute_pbo, which returns 0.0 — the best possible value, clearing every ceiling — when N<2 or T < S*2 = 32 (analytics.py:297-298). compute_pbo_checked exists at analytics.py:208 for exactly this reason ('compute_pbo would return a false-good 0.0 that PASSES the ceiling') and is not used by the MCP. Since the risk MCP is alwaysLoad:true and agents reach for it by default, a short-sample theme candidate gets a silent false PASS through the obvious tool. This is a live defect in the verification path the entire phase depends on.

_NUMERIC_FEATURES IS A FILTER, NOT A REGISTRATION. Verified 37 entries, zero news-derived (consumer_sentiment is FRED UMCSENT). It is used ONLY at backtest_engine.py:712 as `[c for c in _NUMERIC_FEATURES if c in df.columns]`. Values come exclusively from historical_data.build_feature_vector reading three BQ caches with no join and no extension hook. Appending a theme feature name without a build_feature_vector data path is a silent no-op — the exact 'operations that cannot fail loudly' class. Four of the eight lenses describe this integration as a list append.

THE P0 DATA SOURCE IS LICENCE-BLOCKED AND PIT-INVALID, AND FOUR LENSES BUILD ON IT ANYWAY. Alpha Vantage ToS grants rights 'for personal, non-commercial use' and names 'investment analysis, research, testing, monitoring' as triggering commercial use; measured hard cap of 25 requests/day makes a 500-ticker backfill take 400+ days; and the pre-2026 archive is a sparse retroactive backfill (AAPL: 53 articles Jan-2025 vs >=1000 Jan-2026, >=19x discontinuity) so it does not reproduce what a live subscriber would have seen. Lenses 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 all make the AV backfill their FIRST action; Lens 5 measured it as prohibited. Nobody in the corpus reconciled the contradiction.

SELECTING BENEFICIARIES BY NAMING OR COVERAGE IS A PUBLISHED NULL — AND IT IS 83.3'S KILL TEST. Lee/Ozik/Sadka: narrative portfolios formed from the top-25 highest-media-coverage stocks 'do not exhibit abnormal returns'; only return-BETA-selected portfolios earn the 6.96%/yr (t=2.53). This is the same rule ETF issuers use, and Ben-David et al. measure it at -0.50%/mo FFC4 for 60 months (~-30% cumulative), with Appendix Table F.6 confirming a stock-level long of new specialized ETFs' top-5 holdings underperforms similarly, and the worst subset being high pre-launch return AND high media sentiment (-0.53%/mo). 83.3's criterion 'given an AI-datacenter theme fixture the map reaches at least one memory ticker' tests the mechanism the evidence says does not pay.

THE ONE PRO-THESIS RESULT IS HALF AS STRONG AS THE CORPUS STATES. The 6.96%/yr narrative alpha is statistically ZERO in its own first subsample (2013-2017: return 2.53 t=0.49, alpha 1.00 t=0.20) versus 2018-2023 (alpha 9.33, t=3.22) — so it rests on ~5 years of effective evidence, not 10. Its intensity series is proprietary (MKT MediaStats) with two of three authors affiliated to that firm, neither fact disclosed in the corpus. Only 1.46%/yr of the 6.96% is genuinely cross-SECTOR (4.69%/yr is intra-sector, already partly captured by the shipped peer_leadlag overlay), and an independent measurement of AV co-mention edges for MU found essentially every edge inside GICS Information Technology — so the instrument chosen to fix intra-sector myopia measures as intra-sector.

FREE HISTORY IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT; INDEPENDENT EPISODES AND TRIAL COUNT ARE. GDELT's measured 11.46-year window (4,169 daily partitions, unlimited commercial licence) holds only ~23-46 independent cross-sector thematic episodes at 2-4/year — the operator's own four reference cases are 4 episodes in 6 years. At the live purge horizon of 135 days (backtest_engine.py:665, 1.5 x holding_days=90), a 4.4-year corpus collapses to ~12 independent label spans. And the DSR hurdle is driven by TRIAL COUNT, not sample length: extending history from 4.4y to 41y barely moves it, while the corpus enumerates 6+ free parameters (0.7 merge, lambda=0.01, P10/P50 bands, 5-day innovation window, 24/3-month entropy offset, proximity N) before any signal exists. Critically, the trial-Sharpe dispersion V that dominates this arithmetic was ASSUMED (Lens 7 used 0.5, Lens 5 implicitly ~0.30) and MEASURED BY NOBODY — it swings the required Sharpe from 1.38 to 3.18 and the two lenses reached opposite conclusions on it.

THREE POINT-IN-TIME DEFECTS ARE ALREADY LIVE AND WOULD SILENTLY CORRUPT ANY BACKFILL. backend/news/fetcher.py:99 reads `published_at=str(raw.get('published_at') or _now_iso())` — a source omitting a publication time gets stamped with the current wall clock, so a backfill stamps 2022 articles with the 2026 run date and destroys the timeline with no error. Line 100 sets `fetched_at=_now_iso()` unconditionally, so backfilled rows carry the backfill clock as if it were an ingest event, and there is no provenance column distinguishing live from backfill. Separately backend/backtest/data_ingestion.py:229 writes today's yfinance sector onto every historical fundamentals row, which historical_data.py:265 feeds to the model as features['sector'] and peer_leadlag_screen.py groups on. And backend/tools/screener.py::get_sp500_tickers raises NotImplementedError for any historical as_of, so the UNIVERSE itself is survivorship-biased before theme membership is even considered.

design_decision.theme_representation: VERSIONED, FROZEN-AT-BIRTH, APPEND-ONLY registry — never re-fitted, never relabelled. Primary rail is keyword + confirmation-gate (option d), because it is the only representation with a published human-validation number (GPR correlates 0.93 annually with an index built by hand-coding 7,000+ articles), the only one that is point-in-time by construction with no fitting step to leak, and it is already the shape defense_signal.py ships. A theme object carries theme_id, definition_version, birth_date, nullable death_date, trigger/keyword spec, membership set, and an intensity series; ANY change to the spec mints a NEW theme_id with a supersedes pointer and the prior series is never rewritten. Intensity is an attention SHARE (self-normalizing, so news-volume growth cannot masquerade as theme growth) and the tradable quantity is the 6-MONTH intensity DIFFERENCE (trailing 6-month mean minus prior 6-month mean), not article counts — Tetlock measures a 413bps fresh-vs-stale initial-reaction gap that reverses, so counting volume buys repetition of already-priced stories. REJECTED as the live rail: BERTopic (its dynamic mode achieves stable identity only by fitting global topics over the whole corpus and reusing global IDF per timestep — look-ahead by construction; HDBSCAN cannot do incremental updates; 3 new deps not installed), per-cycle LLM labelling (perturbing sample or prompt drops agreement to purity 0.67-0.70 / ARI 0.59-0.63, silently re-partitioning ~1/3 of the corpus and rewriting history in a backtest), and re-estimated LDA (between-run partitions differ from within-run across all three standard similarity measures, so cross-vintage matching is a research project, not a feature). LDA is retained ONLY as a proposal generator whose output is frozen on promotion. Registry entry #1 is GEOPOLITICAL RISK via the Caldara-Iacoviello series — it is CC-BY, free daily since 1985, already fetched at backend/services/macro_regime.py, and its consumer helper _apply_gpr_tilt is already generic over its trigger dict and already serves two themes. MANDATORY: consume DATED VINTAGE files, never the live file — the publisher states values are revised backward, and there is a 2021 search-term methodology break that must be modelled as a regime split.
design_decision.beneficiary_mapping: SELECT BY RETURN BETA TO THE THEME-INTENSITY SERIES. Do NOT select by naming, by article mention count, or by asking an LLM who benefits. This is the single most evidence-backed decision available: coverage-selected narrative portfolios show NO abnormal return while beta-selected ones earn 6.96%/yr (t=2.53); GPT-5 zero-shot scores accuracy 0.555 / F 0.189 on a BALANCED supply-link benchmark against FactSet ground truth (a coin flip); and naming-based selection is exactly what ETF issuers do, measured at -0.50%/mo FFC4 for 60 months with the stock-level top-5-holdings variant underperforming similarly. It is also computationally free here — 500-1000 names x ~50 themes x rolling 26-week windows is seconds in numpy. EXCLUDE the first-order named firm entirely: its underreaction coefficient is 0.939 (t=1.53, not distinguishable from 1) with insignificant post-event CAR (+0.442%, t=1.59) — it prices its own shock within the event month, leaving nothing to harvest. The second-order linked firm covers only ~60% in month 0 (URC 0.600, t=5.71) and closes the rest over t+1..t+6 (CAR +2.799%, t=3.74) — but for OUR universe plan for the large-cap profile: large firms cover 69% in month 0, leaving only 31% residual. The corroboration map (news co-mention, VTNIC vertical relatedness, thematic-ETF co-membership) is a FILTER on beta-selected candidates, never the selector. Explicitly DO NOT BUILD a Cohen-Frazzini customer-momentum overlay: post-2005 value-weighted alpha is 0.62%/mo t=1.54 (insignificant), only ~232 US firms/month have a public customer link at $1.5B average cap (below our universe floor), and the effect is subsumed by analyst-co-coverage momentum (4-factor alpha falls 0.97 t=2.47 to 0.43 t=1.09). Also DO NOT use Hoberg-Phillips TNIC — its own readme states it is 'purged for vertical relationships from the input/output tables', so it returns COMPETITORS, not beneficiaries. Add a hard ENTRY EXCLUSION: candidates in the top quartile of BOTH trailing return and media sentiment are the -0.53%/mo regime and must be excluded from new BUYs regardless of theme intensity.
design_decision.entry_exit_timing: ENTER ON ACCELERATION, NEVER ON BIRTH AND NEVER ON CONFIRMATION. Trigger on a POSITIVE and RISING 6-month attention-intensity difference. Birth is contraindicated: news novelty forecasts a -2.821% year-ahead market return per standard deviation and carries a negative cross-sectional risk premium, so 'a theme is being born' is a BEARISH aggregate signal — the money is cross-sectional selection among beneficiaries, never directional timing of the theme. Confirmation is contraindicated: by the time an issuer launches a thematic ETF the valuation cycle has already peaked (-0.50%/mo FFC4 for the following 60 months). Short-window intensity changes are also out — only the 6-month difference generates the spread; 1-week and 3-month differences do not. EXIT ON A CLOCK, NOT ON THE SIGNAL. Hard exit at 6 months (the second-order gap closes over t+1..t+6; the narrative signal is calibrated at a 6-month hold; the pure-news optimal lookback is 6 months), absolute cap 12 months (predictable returns 'persist for about a year and then fade away'; drift reverses by year 2). MINIMUM HOLDING PERIOD >= 8 WEEKS, TIME-BASED. A signal-based exit makes turnover a function of signal noise and is the single mechanism that converts a slow design into a fast one — the empirical shape of that failure is short-term reversal at 305%/mo turnover, 6.75%/yr cost, capacity $9.5bn, marginal significance. IMPLEMENT AS A SCORE OVERLAY ON THE EXISTING MONTHLY RECONSTITUTION, not a separate event-triggered sleeve: incremental turnover is then ~1.9x NAV/yr costing 3-19 bps/yr, a rounding error, versus 460.7x NAV/yr and 1,382 bps/yr for a daily headline design against a measured value-weighted large-cap alpha budget of 4 bps/month (SE 3, statistically indistinguishable from zero). Separate EVALUATION cadence from TRADING cadence — Lens 4 rejects weekly trading on cost while Lens 5 rejects monthly on CSCV mechanics; both are satisfied by evaluating more finely than you trade. Crowding kill-switch, forced regardless of holding age: a thematic ETF launching on the theme, the intensity difference turning negative (descending-attention narratives are the SHORT leg), or basket media sentiment rolling over from its peak.
design_decision.data_sources: GDELT gkg_partitioned + Caldara-Iacoviello GPR + SEC EDGAR full-text. NOT Alpha Vantage. GDELT: licence is verbatim 'unlimited and unrestricted use for any academic, commercial, or governmental use of any kind without fee'; measured 4,169 daily partitions spanning 2015-02-17 to 2026-08-04 (~99.6% calendar completeness), covering ALL FOUR reference cases including COVID and Ukraine. HARD RULE: always query gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.gkg_partitioned with a _PARTITIONTIME filter (379 MB/day); NEVER gdeltv2.gkg, where one V2Themes query scans 1.88 TB and LIMIT does not reduce cost. Use for AGGREGATE theme intensity ONLY, never firm-level events — the peer-reviewed comparison explicitly endorses that split (positive recall as low as 0.111, precision 0.144 at stressed nodes), and event-level use would recreate the call_transcript_gpr.py failure mode. Deduplicate before use: the ~20.6% redundancy is virality-correlated, i.e. a BIAS not averaging noise. GPR: CC-BY, daily since 1985, 44 countries, already fetched — but consume DATED VINTAGES and treat the 2021 methodology break as a regime split. EDGAR: the sleeper. Public domain, measured floor 2001, 10 req/s (~864k/day, ~1000x our need), filings immutable once accessioned — the best point-in-time integrity of anything assessed, and the only free source that is simultaneously deep, PIT-clean, firm-level and unrestricted. Requires a declaring User-Agent (measured: empty UA returns 403, declared UA returns 200). FRED via ALFRED VINTAGES for macro controls (1,221 INDPRO vintages back to 1927). ALPHA VANTAGE IS AN OPERATOR DECISION, currently treated as BLOCKED: licence restricts to 'personal, non-commercial use' with 'investment analysis, research, testing' named as commercial; measured 25 requests/day; >=19x archive-vs-live density discontinuity making it PIT-invalid regardless of licence. The key IS present in backend/.env, so this needs an explicit written 'do not use' decision, not silence. Alpaca is live-forward-collection only (measured 2015 floor, headlines-only archive with hasContent=False on 2016 rows, and no derived-works licence grant found). Wikipedia pageviews: REJECT as an alpha signal — index-level, contrarian in sign, concentrated in 2008, gross of costs, and the modern API floor (2015-07-01) does not overlap the founding study window at all. Wikipedia EDIT counts: reject outright on two null results (p>0.9 and p=0.19). BigQuery spend is NOT free by assumption — the 1 TiB/month tier is per-billing-account and already shared with pyfinagent_data, pyfinagent_hdw, pyfinagent_pms and financial_reports production workloads; the ~1.58 TB one-time GDELT backfill must be measured against current consumption and operator-approved, not footnoted as $0.
design_decision.expected_sample_adequacy: HONEST ANSWER: NO — not for a gate-grade DSR/PBO verdict on a single theme time series, and the reason is NOT calendar length, so 'find a longer archive' is the wrong remedy. Four multiplicative constraints. (1) OVERLAPPING LABELS: at the live purge horizon of 135 days (backtest_engine.py:665), a 4.4-year corpus yields ~12 independent label spans and GDELT's 11.46 years ~30; a 90-day label inflates naive t-stats by ~sqrt(90) ~= 9.5x. (2) TRIAL COUNT DOMINATES THE DSR HURDLE, and the threshold SR* = V x E[max_N] is INDEPENDENT OF T — so below a floor set by trial dispersion and trial count, no sample length ever clears the gate. Cutting N from 45 to 10 moves the floor far more than extending history from 4.4y to 41y does. (3) THE REAL CEILING IS PBO <= 0.20 (gate.py:22), 2.5x tighter than the 0.50 every lens assumed. (4) CSCV NEEDS >= 10 DIVERSE COMPETING CONFIGURATIONS (analytics.py: PBO_MIN_TRIALS_GATE_GRADE=10, columns_diverse requires pairwise corr_mean < 0.99); a single theme design supplies ONE configuration, and phase-82.3 already measured K=8 columns correlating 0.967-0.979 — non-informative. Against a realistic large-cap net theme alpha of 2-4%/yr at 8-12% vol (Sharpe 0.17-0.50), derived by haircutting Lens 3's 7%/yr gross by the McLean-Pontiff LARGE-CAP-WORST-CASE decay (post-publication decline is greatest in exactly large, liquid, low-idio-vol, dividend-paying stocks — our universe is the worst case, not the average), against a measured breadth ceiling of ~1.4-1.5 GROSS Sharpe for an ~800-name universe, the gap to any plausible requirement is 4-10x. THE DECISIVE CAVEAT, which is why this is a descope and not a kill: the trial-Sharpe dispersion V that drives all of this arithmetic was ASSUMED BY EVERY LENS AND MEASURED BY NONE — Lens 7 used 0.5, Lens 5 implicitly ~0.30, and they reached OPPOSITE conclusions ('unreachable' vs 'history is not the constraint') purely on that undisclosed input. The required Sharpe swings 1.38 to 3.18 across V in {0.25, 1.00}. Measuring V empirically from the realized dispersion of Sharpes across an actually-run trial set is cheap, needs no news corpus, and is the single action that converts this from an argument into a decision — which is why new step 83.1.1 exists and why nothing downstream should be built before it closes. The honest structural ceiling that no amount of data or money fixes: ~23-46 independent cross-sector thematic EPISODES in GDELT's window (the operator's own four reference cases are 4 episodes in 6 years). Rows are plentiful; episodes are not. A DSR computed on daily returns will look far more significant than ~30 effective episodes justify, so the unit of analysis must be reported at the EPISODE level alongside any return-level figure.

revised_criteria: the migration is run and a test asserts the resulting news_articles schema contains BOTH a `published_at` TIMESTAMP column and a distinct `ingested_at` TIMESTAMP column, failing if either is absent or if the two resolve to the same column name

the schema carries a REQUIRED `provenance` STRING column, and a test asserts a row produced by the live fetch path records provenance='live' while a row produced by a backfill path records provenance='backfill', failing if either path leaves it null or if both paths emit the same value

a test injects an insert failure into the fail-open path and asserts the failure BOTH increments an observable counter AND emits a log record, while the writer still returns normally rather than raising -- both halves asserted in the same test

step_changes.rationale: Three research findings force changes. (1) The dominant backtest risk is theme IDENTITY, not theme signal: unsupervised topic models churn violently between runs (BERTopic: only 16% unique values across 342 runs, topic-name stability Rho=-0.06 p=0.7137; LDA between-run partitions differ from within-run across all three standard similarity measures), so the registry must FREEZE definitions at birth and version rather than re-fit -- BERTrend's retained-first-occurrence anchor is the specific anti-drift mechanism. (2) The only theme with enough free history to matter today is geopolitical risk (CC-BY, daily since 1985, already fetched at backend/services/macro_regime.py, with the consumer helper _apply_gpr_tilt already generic and already serving two themes) -- so seeding the registry with it is both the cheapest and the highest-sample-power start. (3) Lens 5 measured that the GPR publisher silently back-revises published history and changed methodology in 2021, so consuming the live file instead of a dated vintage injects lookahead into the one series we were counting on. The original step's implicit LLM-per-cycle assumption is also unnecessary under a keyword+confirmation-gate representation.
step_changes.revised_name: THEME_REGISTRY + point-in-time theme-intensity series, built strictly from $0 sources, with definitions FROZEN AT BIRTH. Generalises backend/services/defense_signal.py -- which its own docstring calls a 'reference-case signal', one hard-coded theme gated on GPR-Acts AND XAR 5-day momentum, default OFF -- into N versioned themes. RESEARCH-DRIVEN CORRECTION TO THE REPRESENTATION: the dominant backtest risk is theme IDENTITY, not theme signal. Measured run-to-run instability of unsupervised topic models is severe (BERTopic: only 16% unique values across 342 runs; topic-name stability against anything Rho=-0.06, p=0.7137; LDA's between-run partition differs from its within-run partition across Jensen-Shannon, Jaccard and Rank-Based-Overlap alike), so a registry that re-fits its definitions each cycle is comparing different objects across windows. Therefore: a theme's DEFINITION is frozen at birth and NEVER re-fitted; any change to the keyword specification or anchor mints a NEW theme_id carrying a supersedes pointer, and the prior series is never rewritten. The primary representation is keyword + confirmation-gate -- the only family with a published human-validation number (0.93 annual correlation against an index built by hand-coding 7,000+ articles) and the only one that is point-in-time by construction with no fitting step to leak. It is also the shape defense_signal.py already ships. REGISTRY ENTRY #1 IS GEOPOLITICAL RISK, not a discovered theme: it is CC-BY licensed, free and daily since 1985, already fetched at backend/services/macro_regime.py, and its consumer helper _apply_gpr_tilt is already generic over its trigger dict and already serves two themes. MANDATORY POINT-IN-TIME RULE, MEASURED 2026-08-04: the publisher states values are revised backward ('in some cases there could be minor revisions of the data extending further back') and that the search terms were last changed in 2021 with a different methodology from the prior index -- so the series MUST be read from a DATED VINTAGE file, never the live file, and the 2021 break must be modelled as a regime split rather than a continuous series. REGRESSION ANCHOR: the defense reference case must reproduce as a registry entry over a fixture spanning the Ukraine-invasion window. step_changes.rationale: The step's kill test is built on a premise the research refutes. Its criterion 'given an AI-datacenter theme fixture the map reaches at least one memory ticker' tests beneficiary selection BY NAMING, which is a published NULL: coverage-selected narrative portfolios show no abnormal return while beta-selected ones earn 6.96%/yr (t=2.53); GPT-5 scores accuracy 0.555 / F 0.189 on a balanced supply-link benchmark against FactSet ground truth; and naming-selection is exactly what ETF issuers do, measured at -0.50%/mo FFC4 for 60 months with the stock-level top-5-holdings variant underperforming similarly. Separately, the instrument the corpus recommends for the cross-sector hop measures as intra-sector: an independent pull of co-mention edges for MU found essentially every edge inside GICS Information Technology, consistent with Lens 3's measurement that only 1.46%/yr of the 6.96%/yr is genuinely cross-sector against 4.69%/yr intra-sector (already partly captured by the shipped peer_leadlag overlay). So the criterion must become a MEASURED cross-sector delta against the existing overlay, not a naming test, and not a threshold on data we have not seen.
step_changes.revised_name: Cross-sector beneficiary SELECTION, corrected by research: select by RETURN BETA to the theme-intensity series, not by naming and not by mention count. MEASURED GAP THAT REMAINS TRUE: a grep for supply_chain|beneficiar|second_order|theme_map|value_chain across backend/services and backend/tools returns NOTHING, and backend/services/peer_leadlag_screen.py groups by GICS sector (lines 75-82, dropping sector-less tickers entirely) so it structurally cannot express a cross-sector hop. RESEARCH-DRIVEN CORRECTION TO THE MECHANISM: the original kill test -- can the map NAME memory from an AI theme -- tests the selection rule the evidence refutes. Narrative portfolios formed from the highest-media-coverage stocks 'do not exhibit abnormal returns'; only return-beta-selected portfolios earn the 6.96%/yr (t=2.53). Asking a frontier model directly is worse: GPT-5 zero-shot scores accuracy 0.555 and F 0.189 on a BALANCED supply-link benchmark against FactSet ground truth -- a coin flip. And naming-selection is precisely what ETF issuers do, measured at -0.50%/month FFC4 for 60 months (~-30% cumulative), with the paper's own stock-level variant -- long the top five holdings of recently-launched specialized ETFs -- showing 'a similar magnitude of underperformance', and the WORST subset being names with high pre-launch returns AND high media sentiment (-0.53%/month). SO: statistics pick the names, the LLM at most defines the theme vocabulary, and a corroboration map (news co-mention, vertical relatedness, thematic-ETF co-membership) acts only as a FILTER on beta-selected candidates. EXCLUDE the first-order named firm entirely -- its underreaction coefficient is 0.939 (t=1.53, not distinguishable from 1) with an insignificant post-event CAR of +0.442% (t=1.59), so it prices its own shock within the event month and has no residual drift to harvest; the second-order linked firm is where the drift lives (URC 0.600, t=5.71; CAR t+1..t+6 of +2.799%, t=3.74), though for a large-cap universe expect the faster profile (large firms close 69% in month 0, leaving 31%). PHASE KILL POINT, RESTATED AS A MEASUREMENT: the question is not whether the map can name memory, it is whether the produced link set carries cross-sector content the existing intra-sector overlay does not. An independent measurement of news co-mention edges for a memory name found essentially every edge inside GICS Information Technology, and only 1.46%/yr of the published 6.96%/yr narrative alpha is genuinely cross-sector against 4.69%/yr intra-sector. Record the measured cross-sector share for both this map and peer_leadlag_screen over the same fixture; the kill decision is made against the 83.1.1 kill rule using that recorded number, not against a threshold invented here. DO NOT build a Cohen-Frazzini customer-momentum overlay: post-2005 value-weighted alpha is 0.62%/mo (t=1.54, insignificant), only ~232 US firms/month have a public customer link at $1.5B average market cap (below this universe's floor), and the effect is subsumed by an analyst-coverage factor requiring paid I/B/E/S (4-factor alpha falls from 0.97 t=2.47 to 0.43 t=1.09). DO NOT use Hoberg-Phillips TNIC as the beneficiary map: its own readme states it is 'purged for vertical relationships from the input/output tables', so it returns COMPETITORS, not beneficiaries. MONEY CONTRIBUTION: selection method is where this phase most plausibly loses money -- the naive version of this step is a measured negative-alpha strategy.

step_changes.revised_name: Make the theme signal BACKTESTABLE: add theme-derived numeric features with a REAL data path, purge on the theme's own horizon, and run an EXECUTABLE contamination diagnostic. MEASURED CORRECTION TO THE INTEGRATION: _NUMERIC_FEATURES at backend/backtest/backtest_engine.py:50-60 holds exactly 37 entries with zero news-derived ones, but it is used ONLY as a column FILTER at line 712 (`[c for c in _NUMERIC_FEATURES if c in df.columns]`); the values come exclusively from backend/backtest/historical_data.py::build_feature_vector reading three BigQuery caches, with no join and no extension hook. Appending a name to the list without a matching key in build_feature_vector is a SILENT NO-OP -- the operations-that-cannot-fail-loudly class. A theme feature therefore requires a point-in-time source, a cache accessor, a build_feature_vector assignment, the list entry, AND a stationarity decision: _build_predict_features (lines 594-625) median-NEUTRALIZES every feature in _NON_STATIONARY at predict time, so a level-valued theme intensity would carry zero cross-sectional signal live while appearing healthy in training. POINT-IN-TIME RULE: features are computed from the publication timestamp, never the ingest timestamp -- using ingestion time leaks our own collection schedule into history, which is exactly what 83.0.1 makes checkable. PURGE ON THE THEME'S HORIZON, NOT THE TRADER'S: the engine purges at `int(self.holding_days * 1.5)` (line 665), which is the exit rule, but a theme's label span is a property of the theme's persistence and under-purges whenever the theme outlives the position. MEASURED CORRECTION TO THE LOOKAHEAD DEFENCE: the LAP interaction test requires first-token log-probabilities at the answer position. The Anthropic and Gemini API rails do not expose them in that shape, and the operator's measured local-LLM verdict (13.7 of 16GB already in use, only 4B-class models fit, with 8B-class finance accuracy at 30-47% against Gemini's 92%) means a local substitute would not be a meaningful measurement. LAP is therefore NOT a mandatory acceptance test here -- writing an unexecutable check into immutable criteria would make this step permanently uncloseable. The executable substitute is the vintage-difference decomposition, which needs no log-probabilities: score the same text with a model vintage predating the article and with the current vintage, and the difference IS the lookahead premium. Restricting the primary evaluation window to strictly after any scoring model's knowledge cutoff remains required, because it eliminates the bias by construction. Reassuring context: in the architecture used here -- text to embeddings to a separately-fit cross-sectional model -- measured contamination is small (chronologically-consistent 4.80 versus contaminated 4.90 long-short Sharpe, p=0.630), so the risk concentrates in ASKING A MODEL FOR A RETURN, not in using one to represent text. THE SIGN REGIME IS A CORRECTNESS BUG, NOT A STYLE CHOICE. MEASURED: settings.sign_safe_overlays defaults False (backend/config/settings.py:37), whose own docstring states the legacy `base*mult` path 'INVERTS on negative momentum composites in drawdowns'. A theme BOOST shipped under that default would therefore make a -10 composite into -10.5 -- WORSE rank -- and would demote theme beneficiaries during exactly the four episodes this phase exists to capture (COVID crash, Ukraine invasion, Iran/oil spike, AI drawdowns). The backtest would never surface it, because the backtest does not run overlays at all. Resolve it explicitly: either force sign_safe_mult(enabled=True) for this overlay -- precedent exists, backend/tools/screener.py already forces it for the soft sector-diversity shading so a penalty cannot invert -- or block the overlay while the global flag is OFF. killed_options: ALPHA VANTAGE NEWS_SENTIMENT AS THE HISTORICAL CORPUS -- killed on three independent, individually-fatal grounds, any one of which suffices. (1) Licence: the Terms of Service grant rights 'for personal, non-commercial use' and list commercial-use triggers including 'You intend to use the Alpha Vantage Platform for any purpose that goes beyond personal usage including investment analysis, research, testing, monitoring' -- our exact use case is named. (2) Rate: the live API returned 'our standard API rate limit is 25 requests per day', making a 500-ticker backfill take 400+ days at a physically impossible one call per ticker. (3) Point-in-time integrity: AAPL returned 53 indexed articles for Jan-2025 versus >=1000 for Jan-2026, a >=19x density discontinuity proving the pre-2026 archive is a sparse retroactive backfill that does not reproduce what a live subscriber would have seen. Note this REVERSES the phase-83 goal's premise that a present key made the source usable, and it disqualifies the P0 action that Lenses 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 all independently proposed. The key IS present in backend/.env, so this needs an explicit written operator decision, not silence.

REUSING scripts/risk/gauntlet.py AS THE PROMOTION GATE (83.5's original instruction) -- killed by the file's own docstring: 'dry-run is currently the ONLY implemented mode. run() refuses non-dry-run invocations with NotImplementedError until the real backtest engine is wired in, and the report writer refuses any report not labeled dry_run: true -- every data path in this script is the seeded stub.' _run_regime_stub emits rng.normal(loc=0.0003, scale=0.018) synthetic returns with no strategy input and sets bt_drawdown equal to drawdown so the evaluator ratio is 1.0 and passes by construction, and the downstream stub-fingerprint check then correctly rejects such a report -- a closed loop that can only produce reports it will itself reject. Separately backend/backtest/gauntlet/evaluator.py runs four gates that are ALL drawdown or kill-switch conditions with zero DSR, zero PBO, zero cost, zero incumbent. Replaced by backend/autoresearch/gate.py::PromotionGate, the module that actually joins DSR and PBO.

PBO <= 0.50 AS THE RESEARCH PROMOTION CEILING -- killed by direct measurement. backend/autoresearch/gate.py:22 sets max_pbo = 0.20 on the class whose evaluate() decides research promotion. The 0.50 figure that all eight research lenses quoted is backend/services/promotion_gate.py:37, which governs a different decision (live allocation staging, keyed on PSR not DSR), and the risk MCP's DEFAULT_PBO_VETO_THRESHOLD is a third, advisory 0.5. Every feasibility verdict in the corpus was therefore computed against a ceiling 2.5x more permissive than the binding one. The divergence of three thresholds across three modules with no cross-reference is itself a defect worth surfacing to the operator.

SELECTING THEME BENEFICIARIES BY NAMING, MENTION COUNT, OR ASKING AN LLM WHO BENEFITS -- killed by a direct published null plus two corroborating negatives. Narrative-mimicking portfolios formed from the top-25 highest-media-coverage stocks 'do not exhibit abnormal returns', while return-beta-selected portfolios earn 6.96%/yr FF6 alpha (t=2.53). GPT-5 zero-shot scores accuracy 0.555 / F 0.189 against FactSet ground truth on a BALANCED 50/50 supply-link benchmark -- essentially a coin flip; DeepSeek-V3.1 F=0.138, GPT-4o F=0.268, versus a trained model at F=0.854. And naming-selection is the rule ETF issuers use, measured at -0.50%/month FFC4 for 60 months (~-30% cumulative), with Appendix Table F.6 confirming a stock-level long of newly-launched specialized ETFs' top-five holdings shows 'a similar magnitude of underperformance'. This kills 83.3's original kill test, which asked whether the map can NAME memory from an AI theme.

COHEN-FRAZZINI CUSTOMER-MOMENTUM AS AN OVERLAY -- killed three times over. Post-publication decay: value-weighted long-short falls from 1.30%/mo (t=3.03, 1978-2004) to 0.62%/mo (t=1.54, 2005-2018), i.e. insignificant in the value-weighted implementation this universe requires. Subsumption: the 4-factor alpha collapses from 0.97 (t=2.47) to 0.43 (t=1.09) once shared-analyst-coverage momentum is controlled, and that control needs paid I/B/E/S. Coverage: only ~232 US firms per month have an identifiable public customer link, at $1.5B average market cap -- below a 500-1000 large/mid-cap universe's floor. In the one head-to-head test including transaction costs, customer momentum 'does not yield positive returns or CH-4 alpha' at all and was dropped from the study.

HOBERG-PHILLIPS TNIC AS THE BENEFICIARY MAP -- killed by the dataset's own readme, verbatim: 'Note: TNIC industries are also purged for vertical relationships from the input/output tables.' It returns COMPETITORS, not beneficiaries; using it for a theme-to-supplier hop is a category error, and TNIC3 is the file most people reach for by default. The vertical variant (VTNIC) is free but has never been validated for return prediction, measures POTENTIAL relatedness from vocabulary overlap rather than observed trade, ships at a granularity where ~10% of all random firm pairs are flagged related, and is keyed on gvkey only -- no ticker, no CIK -- with the official crosswalk being a paid WRDS product.

BERTopic AS THE LIVE THEME REPRESENTATION -- killed on three independent grounds: its dynamic-topic mode achieves stable identity only by fitting global topics over the whole corpus and reusing pre-calculated GLOBAL IDF values per timestep, which is look-ahead by construction; the online partial_fit path cannot use HDBSCAN, its default and best clusterer, so going point-in-time means changing the algorithm; and measured run-to-run instability is severe (only 16% unique values across 342 runs; topic-name stability Rho=-0.06, p=0.7137; error size SD +/-4,604.76 on a mean of 56,281.51). It also needs three new dependencies (umap, hdbscan, bertopic) that are not installed, while sklearn 1.8.0 and sentence_transformers 5.5.1 already are.

PER-CYCLE LLM THEME LABELLING AS A LIVE RAIL -- killed on reproducibility and cost. Identical re-runs agree at purity 0.95 / ARI 0.92, but ANY perturbation of the input sample or the prompt drops agreement to purity 0.67-0.70 / ARI 0.59-0.63, meaning roughly a third of the corpus is silently re-partitioned on any input change, which rewrites history inside a backtest. It is also the only option with a recurring metered cost (~$100 per dataset run in the source), violating the $0 constraint, and it degrades catastrophically on affordable local models (Mistral-7B produced 1,418 topics where GPT-3.5 produced 151). Retained ONLY as a one-shot naming step at theme birth whose output is immediately frozen.

MANDATING THE LAP (Lookahead Propensity) TEST AS AN IMMUTABLE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION -- killed as unexecutable on this rail, which would have made 83.4 permanently uncloseable. LAP requires first-token log-probabilities at the answer position; the Anthropic and Gemini API rails do not expose them in that shape, and the operator's measured local-LLM verdict (13.7 of 16GB already in use, only 4B-class models fit, 8B-class finance accuracy 30-47% versus Gemini's 92%) means a local substitute would not constitute a meaningful measurement. Replaced by the vintage-difference decomposition, which needs no log-probabilities. The underlying risk is also smaller than feared in the architecture actually proposed: text-to-embeddings-to-separately-fit-model showed 4.80 versus 4.90 long-short Sharpe (p=0.630, a null) -- contamination concentrates in ASKING A MODEL FOR A RETURN, not in using one to represent text.

ENTITY ANONYMIZATION AS THE LOOKAHEAD CONTROL -- killed as a confounded instrument. Masking company names IMPROVED in-sample returns (+5.89 bps/day on scraped headlines, +4.37 on Thomson Reuters), because the negative 'distraction effect' outweighs the positive look-ahead gain; out-of-sample the difference is p=0.23 (null) and p=0.064 (borderline). A second source notes anonymization's information loss 'can be more severe than the look-ahead bias it seeks to address'.

RAW ALPHA-DECAY (in-sample minus out-of-sample) AS THE CONTAMINATION METRIC -- killed by its own source's controls: a Mean Reversion baseline decayed -10.78pp and a RANDOM NOISE control decayed -10.30pp between the same two windows, versus -15 to -22pp for the allegedly-contaminated models. Regime change alone produces double-digit decay, so a decay figure is meaningless without a matched zero-information control over identical windows.

FAST HEADLINE-DRIFT TRADING -- killed with a number attached, confirming the operator's prior decision rather than relitigating it. Turnover is 460.7x NAV/yr one-way, costing 737 bps/yr at 1.6bps, 1,382 bps/yr at 3bps, and 4,607 bps/yr (46%/yr) at the repo's own 10bps default -- against a measured cost-optimized value-weighted large-cap alpha budget of 4 bps/month (SE 3 bps, statistically indistinguishable from zero). The source's own value-weighted long-short is 10 bps/day gross at 91.4% daily turnover, which at its own published 10bps convention derives to -8.28 bps/day, roughly -21%/yr. Weekly full-book rotation is killed on the same arithmetic (104x NAV/yr, 312 bps/yr at 3bps).

REOPENING BANDING / NO-TRADE BANDS / SCORE HYSTERESIS to make a higher-turnover thematic design affordable -- killed on effect size, not direction. The literature's 41-42% turnover-and-cost reduction is real, but at this book's cost level the entire available saving is roughly 5 bps/yr at 3bps and 16 bps/yr at 10bps, far below any detectable effect on the available sample. The repo already measured dSharpe +0.015, p=0.376, CI90 [-0.066, +0.092] and rejected the family; hysteresis remains banned.

EQUAL-WEIGHTING THE THEMATIC BASKET -- killed on measured cost: equal-weighted transaction costs run 'two to three times as high' as value-weighted because equal-weighting pulls the basket into the illiquid tail, and equal-weighted results 'often result in a deterioration of net performance'. Note the entire documented news effect is a small-cap effect (equal-weighted long-short Sharpe 4.29 versus value-weighted 1.33, a 3.2x concentration), so equal-weighting would be importing a result our universe cannot realise while paying its costs.

WIKIPEDIA PAGEVIEWS AS A THEMATIC ALPHA SIGNAL, AND WIKIPEDIA EDIT COUNTS ENTIRELY -- pageviews killed for that role because the published effect is index-level (DJIA), CONTRARIAN in sign (after a rise in views the DJIA returned -0.0021 the next week, p<0.001; after a fall, +0.0027, p<0.001), concentrated in the 2008 crisis year (0.89 SD versus 0.19 in 2009 and 2010), gross of transaction costs by the authors' own admission, and unreplicable because the modern API floor of 2015-07-01 has ZERO overlap with the 2007-2012 study window. Edit counts killed outright on two null results in the founding paper (p>0.9 and p=0.19).
residual_risks: THE GO/NO-GO ARITHMETIC STILL RESTS ON AN UNMEASURED PARAMETER. Trial-Sharpe dispersion V drives the deflation threshold linearly, and the required annualized Sharpe swings from roughly 1.38 to 3.18 across V in {0.25, 1.00}. Lens 7 assumed 0.5 and concluded the gate is unreachable; Lens 5 implicitly used ~0.30 (and was internally inconsistent across its own six rows) and concluded free history is not the constraint. New step 83.1.1 exists to measure it, but until it closes, every feasibility statement in this decision -- including my own -- is conditional. Do not let 83.1.1's measured V be chosen from the trial set that most flatters the answer; the criterion requires the trial count it was measured over to be recorded alongside it for exactly this reason.

All eight phase-83 steps are status=pending and none has begun, and this revision was explicitly commissioned, so the exception is defensible -- but it must be recorded in handoff/harness_log.md as an operator-sanctioned pre-start revision, not applied silently. THE PRICE-MEDIATED CHANNEL (new step 83.2.1) IS A SCOPE ADDITION ON THIN EVIDENCE. It was surfaced by one adversarial auditor and was researched by ZERO of the eight lenses, so it carries none of the corpus's depth. Its single cited source (commodity price changes predicting industry returns up to six trading weeks, 40 of 49 US industries, 1985-2010) was not read in full by anyone, and that same source reports precious metals as the most prominent channel with energy showing LESS evidence since 1985 -- meaning the operator's oil reference case is the weakest instance, not the strongest. It is queued at P2 behind the go/no-go for that reason. If it survives 83.1.1 it should get its own research gate before it gets code.

THE FOUR REFERENCE CASES ARE STILL NOT TRACED END-TO-END, AND NOBODY IN THE CORPUS DID IT. No lens produced a single walkthrough of detection date, membership set, entry, exit and measured return for any one case. Reference case 2 (AI to datacenter to memory) is the operator's most important and the corpus cannot explain it: the co-mention instrument measures as intra-sector, VTNIC flags ~10% of random pairs, BEA input-output collapses the whole chain into one summary industry at annual granularity, and the LLM route scores F=0.189. One end-to-end walkthrough would falsify more of this design than another literature lens, and 83.1's revised reference-case table criterion forces the source-coverage half of it but not the return half.

83.5 IS LIKELY TO FAIL AND THAT MUST NOT BE TREATED AS A SURPRISE. The honest expectation, stated so it cannot be relitigated later: a realistic large-cap net theme alpha of 2-4%/yr at 8-12% volatility implies Sharpe 0.17-0.50, against a measured breadth ceiling of ~1.4-1.5 GROSS Sharpe for an ~800-name universe and a deflation hurdle materially above that once trial count enters. The operator's standing kill criterion already covers this -- a FAIL stops the phase and cancels 83.6 and 83.7 -- but the pressure to soften will be real precisely because 83.0 through 83.4 will have been genuine work. The 83.1 pre-registration hash guard and the 83.5 criterion requiring the verdict be derived programmatically from the gate module's returned promoted field exist to make softening mechanically visible.
